transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been getting out of breath climbing the stairs, that's the main thing. My wife noticed it too.
When did you first notice it?
It's come on gradually, a while back now I suppose. Hard to put a date on it.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's when I'm doing something — going up the stairs or walking uphill. If I stop and rest a couple of minutes, it settles down again.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
Just puffed out, like I can't get enough air in. It's not pain or anything like that, just breathless.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's just in my chest, I suppose — I don't feel it spreading anywhere. It's not a pain, just being out of puff.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I couldn't really put a number on it. It's not too bad, but it does stop me in my tracks.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
Only when I'm up and about doing something. When I'm sat down resting I'm fine, not breathless at all.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Well, my ankles get a bit puffy by the evening. And I've been needing more pillows to prop myself up at night than I used to.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've got a heart rhythm problem — atrial fibrillation, they told me. Had it about five years now. And I had a heart attack some years back too.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
I take a few tablets for my heart — my wife sorts them out into one of those boxes for me, so I'm not great on the names.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Not that I know of — I've never had a reaction to anything.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Stairs have become a real struggle, and I get puffed going uphill. I never used to be like this.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
It does worry me. I'm wondering whether my heart is getting worse, and how I'll manage getting up the stairs to bed.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
